```{r}
#| label: load
#| include: false
# All data loading + metric math (Q/B/2+2SD, MEF, SI, spectral signature) lives in
# the shared loader, also used by AuroraEVO_6PeakUltra_Dashboard.qmd.
source("pages/_6peak_load.R")
```

Secondary QC for the Cytek Aurora EVO from SPHERO **URCP-38-2K** Ultra Rainbow
beads. The set resolves into **6 populations** — blank particles (peak 1) plus 5
fluorescent rainbow levels (peaks 2–6). **Note on the Aurora:** daily QC adjusts
each APD's *gain* to pin bead MFI to a target, so raw MFI is held ~constant by
design — the informative signals are the ones gain can't compensate:
**sensitivity (2+2SD limit of resolution, Q & B)**, **%CV**, and **linearity**. Heavy FCS processing is done once by
`scripts/Process6PeakUltra.R`; this page reads the `peak_metrics.csv` archive
(+ the daily-QC gain) so it stays light.

```{r}
#| label: prelim-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
if (n_runs < 5) cat(sprintf(
  "::: {.callout-warning appearance='simple'}\nOnly **%d run(s)** so far — trends and the mean ± 2 SD control limits are **preliminary** and will firm up as more runs accumulate.\n:::\n\n", n_runs))
```

# Executive summary

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="Executive summary — run status and latest-vs-baseline overview (click to collapse)"}

```{r}
#| label: run-status
#| results: asis
status <- pm |> filter(peak == n_peaks) |> group_by(run_label) |>
  summarise(saturated = sum(!in_range), total = n(), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(run_label)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(status))) { r <- status[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("::: {.%s}\n**Run %s** — %d / %d detectors saturated at peak 6 (brightest).\n:::\n\n",
              if (r$saturated == 0) "callout-note" else "callout-warning",
              as.character(r$run_label), r$saturated, r$total)) }
```

Latest run vs the baseline run (**`r base_run`**), per detector. Blue = improved,
red = degraded (sign adjusted so red is always *worse*). Hover for values.

```{r}
#| label: overview-heat
latest <- runs[length(runs)]
ov <- metrics |> filter(run_label == latest) |>
  transmute(detector,
            `2+2SD limit`   = -lor_mfi_d,           # lower = better -> flip
            `Sensitivity Q` = Q_d,                 # higher = better -> red when negative
            `Background B`  = -B_d,                 # higher B worse -> flip (B in Spe)
            `Peak-6 %CV`    = -cvt_d,               # higher CV worse -> flip
            `Staining idx`  = si_d,
            `Peaks resolved`= n_resolved_d,
            `MFI/gain`      = mfi_norm_d) |>
  pivot_longer(-detector, names_to = "metric", values_to = "delta")
ov$delta[!is.finite(ov$delta)] <- NA
lim <- stats::quantile(abs(ov$delta), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE); if (!is.finite(lim) || lim == 0) lim <- 1
ovp <- ggplot(ov, aes(metric, detector, fill = pmax(pmin(delta, lim), -lim),
                      text = sprintf("%s | %s<br>%+.1f%% vs baseline", detector, metric, delta))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(detector_channels)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#b2182b", mid = "white", high = "#2166ac", midpoint = 0,
                       name = "Δ% vs\nbaseline\n(red=worse)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = sprintf("Detector performance change — %s vs baseline", latest)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8) + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5),
                                  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
gp(ovp, 680)
```

# Detail {.tabset}

## Peak clustering

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Peak clustering — cluster images and cluster sizes (click to expand)"}

The 6 URCP-38-2K populations are assigned **once per run** by model-based clustering
(flowClust, K = 6) on the asinh-transformed anchor detectors, then read out in every
detector. This is far more robust than per-detector peak finding: weak channels
can't resolve dim peaks alone, but the strong anchor detectors can, and a bead's
population label is fixed across all detectors. Labels are ordered 1–6 by ascending
brightness: peak 1 = blank particles, peaks 2–6 = fluorescent rainbow levels.
Clustering runs in `Process6PeakUltra.R`; this page reads the persisted result.

### 2D cluster assignment (V8-A × B9-A)

The per-run diagnostic: each run's gated beads shown on two detectors that both
resolve all 6 peaks. A clean assignment shows **6 tight, ordered, single-coloured
blobs** along the diagonal — blank (peak 1) at the dim end, brightest (peak 6) at
the top — with no interleaving.

```{r}
#| label: cluster2d-images
#| output: asis
clus_imgs <- sort(list.files("images/6peak_ultra_evo", pattern = "^cluster2d_.*[.]png$", full.names = TRUE))
if (length(clus_imgs) == 0) cat("_No saved cluster images yet — run `scripts/Process6PeakUltra.R`._\n\n") else {
  cat("::: {layout-ncol=3}\n")
  for (f in clus_imgs) cat(sprintf("![Run %s](../%s)\n\n", sub("^cluster2d_(.*)[.]png$","\\1",basename(f)), f))
  cat(":::\n")
}
```

### Cluster-size sanity

URCP-38-2K mixes the 6 populations in roughly equal proportions (blank particles
may be slightly more abundant). Cluster sizes should be broadly even — a quick
numeric check that no population was split or merged by the clustering step.

```{r}
#| label: cluster-sizes
#| fig-height: 3
csz <- pm |> group_by(run_label, peak) |>
  summarise(events = mean(n, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(peak = factor(peak, levels = 1:n_peaks))
gp(ggplot(csz, aes(factor(peak), events, fill = run_label,
                   text = sprintf("peak %s | %s<br>mean events %.0f", peak, run_label, events))) +
     geom_col(position = position_dodge()) +
     labs(title = "Cluster size per peak (events per run; peak 1 = blank)",
          x = "Peak", y = "Events", fill = NULL) +
     theme_bw(base_size = 10), 300)
```

## Tracking over time

Each peak's median intensity and %CV against acquisition timestamp — the QC payoff.
Stable lines mean stable performance; a step or drift flags a detector/laser
problem. Resolved, in-range peaks only. These fill in as runs accumulate (sparse,
mostly points, with few timestamps so far).

### Per-laser overview

Two 5-laser × run heatmaps of peak-6 deviation from each detector's baseline (first
run), averaged across the laser. **Top:** median intensity shift (blue = dimmer,
red = brighter). **Bottom:** %rCV shift (blue = tighter, red = broader). A whole-row
shift points to a laser-level issue; an isolated tile flags a single detector.

```{r}
#| label: laser-overview
#| fig-height: 3
p6_base <- pm |> filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range) |> group_by(detector) |>
  slice_min(run_label, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(detector, base_median = median) |> ungroup()
laser_delta <- pm |> filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range) |>
  left_join(p6_base, by = "detector") |>
  mutate(delta_pct = (median - base_median) / base_median * 100,
         laser = factor(laser_of(detector), levels = laser_levels)) |>
  group_by(laser, run_label) |> summarise(delta_pct = mean(delta_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
lim <- max(abs(laser_delta$delta_pct), na.rm = TRUE); if (!is.finite(lim) || lim == 0) lim <- 1
gp(ggplot(laser_delta, aes(run_label, laser, fill = delta_pct,
        text = sprintf("%s laser | %s<br>%+.1f%% vs baseline", laser, run_label, delta_pct))) +
     geom_tile(colour = "white") +
     scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(laser_levels)) +
     scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", midpoint = 0,
                          limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "Peak 6\nΔ median\nvs t0") +
     labs(title = "Per-laser peak-6 median deviation from baseline", x = NULL, y = "Laser") +
     theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
     theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 10)), 420)
```

```{r}
#| label: laser-overview-cv
#| fig-height: 3
p6_base_cv <- pm |> filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range) |> group_by(detector) |>
  slice_min(run_label, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(detector, base_rcv = rcv) |> ungroup()
laser_delta_cv <- pm |> filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range) |>
  left_join(p6_base_cv, by = "detector") |>
  mutate(delta_pct = (rcv - base_rcv) / base_rcv * 100,
         laser = factor(laser_of(detector), levels = laser_levels)) |>
  group_by(laser, run_label) |> summarise(delta_pct = mean(delta_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
lim_cv <- max(abs(laser_delta_cv$delta_pct), na.rm = TRUE); if (!is.finite(lim_cv) || lim_cv == 0) lim_cv <- 1
gp(ggplot(laser_delta_cv, aes(run_label, laser, fill = delta_pct,
        text = sprintf("%s laser | %s<br>%+.1f%% vs baseline rCV", laser, run_label, delta_pct))) +
     geom_tile(colour = "white") +
     scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(laser_levels)) +
     scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", midpoint = 0,
                          limits = c(-lim_cv, lim_cv), name = "Peak 6\nΔ %rCV\nvs t0") +
     labs(title = "Per-laser peak-6 %rCV deviation from baseline", x = NULL, y = "Laser") +
     theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
     theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 10)), 420)
```

## %CV & noise floor

Peak 6 (brightest) uses **robust %CV** — it has a well-defined mean (~1–2% when
healthy). The blank (peak 1) uses its **absolute robust spread** (IQR/1.349), not
%CV: the blank sits near zero, so %CV explodes when the mean dips toward zero even
though the actual spread is unchanged. A rising blank spread is a genuine
noise-floor increase.

```{r}
#| label: cvtop-heat
gp(heat(cvtop, "cvt", "Peak-6 %CV", "brightest population (mean well-defined)"))
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
```{r}
#| label: cv1-heat
gp(heat(cvp1, "sd1", "Peak-1 noise floor", "absolute robust spread (IQR/1.349), not %%CV"))
```

```{r}
#| label: cv1-heat-fc
gp(heat_fc(cvp1, "sd1", "Noise floor — fold-change", "lower is better; red = noisier than its best", higher_better = FALSE))
```
:::

```{r}

  summarise(cvt = mean(cvt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
gp(ggplot(cl_lat, aes(run_label, cvt, colour = laser, group = laser)) +
     geom_line() + geom_point() +
     labs(title = "Mean peak-6 %%CV per laser (± control context as runs accumulate)",
          x = NULL, y = "Peak-6 %%CV") + theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
```

## Brightest peak (peak 6) %CV

A focused per-detector view of peak 6 (the brightest fluorescent level) alone over
time. The brightest population is normally the tightest (~1–2%), so any rise is a
sensitive indicator of saturation, noise, or linearity issues at the top of the
dynamic range. The cross-detector snapshot and per-laser mean are under
**%CV & noise floor**.

## Sensitivity (2+2SD, Q & B)

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**New method (2026-11-11).** Sensitivity now uses the Parks 2017 weighted quadratic
fit and the Parks 2018 **2+2SD limit of resolution**, adopted from the cross-instrument
Sensitivity study. The previous CV²-vs-1/x / STN-17 version is archived in
`_attic/6peak_ultra_v1_2026-11-11/`.
:::

The headline metric is the **2+2SD limit of resolution**: the smallest amount of dye
whose −2 SD edge clears the blank's +2 SD edge. **Lower = more sensitive.** It combines
detection efficiency (Q) and the background noise floor (BSD) into one number, which is
why Parks et al. (2018) recommend it for tracking and comparing instruments. On this
EVO the limit is **background-limited** (the photon 4/Q share is typically 2–5%), so it
is mostly driven by blank noise and is stable run to run (~5–10%).

It is calculated for **all 64 detectors** in as-acquired MFI. Daily QC pins bead MFI to
fixed targets, so the MFI scale is held constant (the URCP MEF-per-MFI factor *k* moves
~2% across all runs, including the v2-gain change). A detector that loses sensitivity
therefore shows up as a **higher limit at the pinned scale**. For the 18 detectors with
a URCP-38-2K certificate assignment it is also reported in **MEF** below.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Method & provenance — read me

Per detector and run, the variance of each bead population (raw MFI) is fit as

`V = c0 + c1·M + c2·M²`

on **all non-saturated peaks, including the blank** (Parks et al., *Cytometry A* 2017;91:232),
by weighted least squares with weights `n / (2·V̂²)`, iterated to convergence.
`c0` is background variance, `c1·M` photon (shot) noise, `c2·M²` the intensity-proportional
spread (bead intrinsic CV + illumination). Per-peak SD is IQR/1.349; for the **blank the
right-half SD (P84 − P50)** is used (Chase & Hoffman 1998), and SDs are used directly —
never `%rCV × median`, which flips sign when a blank median is ≤ 0.

| Quantity | Formula | Units |
|---|---|---|
| **2+2SD** (all detectors) | `4·(c1 + blank SD)` | MFI |
| **2+2SD** (MEF detectors) | `4·(1/Q + BSD)` | MEF |
| Q | `k / c1` (MEF) · `gain / c1` (relative, all detectors) | Spe per MEF · relative |
| B | `c0 / (c1·k)` (MEF) · `c0 / c1²` (all detectors) | MEF · Spe |
| BSD | measured blank SD / *k* (checked against fitted √c0 / *k*, within ~5%) | MEF |
| CV₀ | `√c2` | % |
| *k* | slope-1 log–log fit of median vs certificate MEF, peaks 2–6 | MFI per MEF |

**Validity.** Fits with χ²/df > 50 (weighted residuals vs pure sampling noise; 2–7 is
normal with IQR-based SDs) are **suppressed**, since the model does not describe the data
(listed in the table below). For MEF values the free log–log slope must be **0.9–1.1** with
R² > 0.98; otherwise the certificate's MEF scale does not match that detector (most UV and
violet channels here, slopes 1.15–1.36; PE-Cy5 0.79). Those rows are still shown, flagged as
lower-confidence.

**Caveats.** Q is a *statistical-photoelectron* Q: it includes APD multiplication noise,
so it is not a quantum efficiency, and with only ~500–1,000 events per peak its per-run fit
SE is ~30% — read Q and B as relative trends. Red detectors (APC, APC-Cy7) are lower-confidence
because the dim beads' intrinsic CV is large there (Hoffman & Wood 2007). Each value is
for one raw detector, not sensitivity after unmixing. Full derivation:
`Sensitivity Articles/QB_2plus2SD_method_summary.md`.
:::

### Q & B (relative, all detectors)

Q and B from the same fit, in statistical-photoelectron terms: **Q** = `gain / c1`
(relative detection efficiency, higher = better), **B** = `c0 / c1²` (background in
photoelectrons, lower = better). Both divide by the fitted photon term `c1`, which is
the least precise coefficient (~30% SE per run), so expect more run-to-run scatter here
than in the 2+2SD limit and look for sustained shifts rather than single points.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
```{r}
#| label: q-heat
gp(heat(qb, "Q", "Detection efficiency Q (relative)", "gain / c1 — higher = better"))
```

```{r}
#| label: q-heat-fc
gp(heat_fc(qb, "Q", "Q — fold-change (per detector)", "vs its own best; red = degraded", higher_better = TRUE))
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: b-heat
gp(heat(qb |> filter(is.finite(B), B > 0) |> mutate(`log10 B` = log10(B)), "log10 B",
        "Background B (log₁₀ photoelectrons)", "c0 / c1² — higher = more background"))
```


### Linearity

**MEF-calibrated** (SPHERO URCP-38-2K) for the 18 certificate detectors, plus a
rank-based R² overview for all 64. On the log–log fit a slope ≠ 1 means the detector
does not match the certificate's MEF assignment (spectral mismatch); curvature flags
compression or saturation (bright end) or floor effects (dim end). The certificate's
5 fluorescent peaks map directly to data peaks 2–6 (peak 1 = blank, unassigned).

```{r}
#| label: lin-mef
#| eval: !expr has_mef
#| fig-height: 6.5
ld <- lin_mef |> filter(run_label == max(run_label)) |> mutate(panel = paste0(fluor, " (", detector, ")"))
gp(ggplot(ld, aes(MEF, median)) +
     geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.4) +
     geom_point(aes(text = sprintf("data peak %s<br>MEF %.0f<br>MFI %.0f", peak, MEF, median)), size = 1.3) +
     scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
     facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
     labs(title = sprintf("MEF-calibrated linearity — %s", max(lin_mef$run_label)),
          x = "Assigned MEF (URCP-38-2K)", y = "Measured MFI") +
     theme_bw(base_size = 8), 600)
```

```{r}
#| label: lin-mef-table
#| eval: !expr has_mef
qb_mef |> group_by(detector) |> arrange(run_label) |>
  summarise(Fluorophore = dplyr::first(fluor),
            `slope (~1)` = round(dplyr::last(ll_slope), 2),
            `R2` = round(dplyr::last(ll_r2), 4),
            `k (MFI/MEF)` = signif(dplyr::last(k), 3),
            `MEF OK` = ifelse(dplyr::last(mef_ok), "yes", "**no**"),
            `2+2SD (MEF)` = signif(dplyr::last(lor), 3),
            `2+2SD Δ% vs base` = round((dplyr::last(lor) - dplyr::first(lor)) / dplyr::first(lor) * 100, 1),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(match(detector, detector_channels)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Per-detector linearity, MEF scale and 2+2SD (latest run). Lower 2+2SD = more sensitive.")
```

#### Rank-based overview (all detectors)

```{r}
#| label: lin-heat
gp(heat(lin, "r2", "Linearity R² (log MFI vs peak rank)", "1 = perfectly log-linear"))
```

### Gain context

**MFI/gain**: peak-6 bead intensity with the daily-QC gain divided out. It should be
flat if the bead and optics are stable.

```{r}
#| label: gain-missing-note
#| output: asis
if (length(runs_no_gain)) cat(sprintf(
  "::: {.callout-warning appearance='simple'}\nNo daily-QC gain found in the archive for **%s** — these run(s) are shown blank on every gain-normalised panel (relative Q, MFI/gain, and the executive overview's Q & MFI rows) rather than mixed onto a raw-MFI scale. Their other metrics (2+2SD, B, MEF-unit values, linearity, %%CV) are unaffected and fully valid. Update `data/EVO/Archive/ArchivedDataEVO.csv` with the run's gain to populate the gain panels.\n:::\n\n",
  paste(runs_no_gain, collapse = ", ")))
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
```{r}
#| label: mfinorm-heat
#| eval: !expr has_gain
gp(heat(ptop, "mfi_norm", "Peak-6 MFI / gain", "absolute — gain-removed intensity"))
```

```{r}
#| label: mfinorm-heat-fc
#| eval: !expr has_gain
gp(heat_fc(ptop, "mfi_norm", "MFI/gain — fold-change", "vs its own best; red = dimmer", higher_better = TRUE))
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: no-gain
#| eval: !expr '!has_gain'
#| output: asis
cat("_No matching daily-QC gain found for these runs (data/EVO/Archive/ArchivedDataEVO.csv) — gain context unavailable, so Q/B and MFI use raw MFI._\n")
```
